title: Investigate GPU KV-cache pollution causing slot starvation and implement KV-aware admission + tenant pacing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity incident on 2025-02-09 we observed long tail queue build-up and persistent GPU slot exhaustion despite autoscaler activity. Post-incident telemetry points to heavy KV-cache churn (frequent evictions and large cache rehydration costs) driven by short-lived tenant bursts and large batched requests. This churn appears to amplify queue buildup because requests that miss the KV cache impose much higher per-request GPU work, causing slot starvation for normal traffic. Goal: validate KV-cache pollution as a primary contributor and implement a mitigation that combines KV-aware admission control (prefer small-cache-friendly requests when pool pressure is high) and tenant pacing (softly rate-limits tenants that cause repeated heavy cache churn) to reduce tail latency and avoid pool-wide exhaustion.
implementation_plan: 1) Reproduce: build a synthetic tenant-burst load generator that mimics observed request mixes (large prompt lengths, many unique prefixes) and run against a staging GPU pool to reproduce KV churn and slot starvation.

2) Telemetry: add short-term histograms to runtime for KV cache hit/miss per-request, eviction rates per-shard, and per-tenant cache churn score. Instrument admission controller with pool pressure signal and cache-aware scoring.

3) Design: finalize KV-aware admission policy that scores incoming requests by expected KV cost (estimated miss penalty = expected reconstruction tokens * kernel-cost-factor) and admission budget per-slot. Define tenant pacing policy: exponential backoff + token bucket with decay keyed by per-tenant churn score.
4) Prototype: implement KV-score estimation in admission controller and a lightweight tenant pacing middleware; add feature flags to enable per-pool gradual rollout.
5) Canary: roll out to a small dedicated pool with synthetic blast tests and 48h soak; monitor GPU utilization, queue lengths, P95/P99 latency, and cost metrics.
6) Rollout: staged rollout with metrics gates; update autoscaler tuning to account for reduced churn baseline; publish runbook changes and alerts.
7) Post-rollout: run retrospective and update the incident playbook with a new 'KV pollution' checklist and mitigation run commands.
8) Docs: add design doc and example tuning knobs in internal docs (Console runbook + operations playbook).
acceptance_criteria: A) Repro test shows >50% reduction in mean per-request KV rehydration work under representative burst profile.
B) Canonical canary (48h) shows no GPU exhaustion events and a P99 latency improvement of at least 20% on impacted tenants.
C) No more than 3% increase in median latency for normal (non-burst) tenants during canary.
D) New dashboard panels for 'per-tenant cache churn', 'KV miss penalty estimate', and 'admission rejection reasons' exist and are surfaced in Console.
E) Runbook updated and on-call engineers briefed on new mitigation steps; postmortem follow-up closed with stakeholder sign-off.
risks: Admission policy may over-throttle latency-sensitive tenants if scoring is incorrect — must use conservative thresholds and gradual rollout.
Tenant pacing could cause tenant-visible rate limits; need to expose backoff signals in API responses and provide self-service quotas.
Telemetry overhead: fine-grained per-request metrics may increase control-plane and metrics costs — batch/aggregate where possible.
Rollout gating mistakes could create oscillation between autoscaler and admission; coordinate with autoscale team and include hysteresis.
comments: 2025-02-15 - Aisha Raman: Created ticket after initial triage. Observed correlation between KV eviction spikes and GPU queue depth in the 2025-02-09 incident dump. Filed this as a follow-up to reduce recurrence risk.

2025-02-16 - Marco Li: Ran initial synthetic repro in staging. Able to reproduce sustained 90%+ GPU utilization with small number of tenant bursts and measured KV rehydration cost ~3-5x baseline on misses. Captured flame graphs and cache metrics (links below).

2025-02-18 - Design review notes (Sofia Kim): Suggest scoring heuristic: estimated_miss_penalty = avg_missing_kv_keys * mean_rehydration_tokens * seq_token_cost_factor. Recommend starting with a conservative threshold at 2.5x base cost.

2025-02-19 - Marco Li: Prototype KV-score in admission controller (feature flag kv_score_admission). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4021. Prototype includes per-request lightweight estimate (no extra RT lookups) and a tenant pacing token-bucket keyed by tenant_id.

2025-02-21 - Ops feedback (Priya Desai): Need clear telemetry panels and an incident runbook entry before canary. Will coordinate on alert thresholds and grafana dashboard. Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/GPUPool/kvcache-churn?orgId=1
2025-02-24 - Security review (Daniel Ortega): Verified no new secrets or data exfil pathways introduced by telemetry. Marking security_review_required=false.

2025-02-26 - Marco Li: Canary started on pool-pilot-03 behind feature flag. Early results after 24h: eviction rate down 48%, per-request rehydration tokens down 42%, P99 latency for bursty tenants improved 27%. Continuing soak.
2025-02-28 - Aisha Raman: Scheduling brief with SRE and Product to align rollout plan and public customer comms for tenants likely to be paced.
notes: We intentionally avoid evict-on-admission changes that touch model weights or runtime policy; mitigation should live in admission layer and tenant pacing to reduce blast radius.
Longer term: consider a multi-level KV cache (hot small-cache per-tenant + shared pool) and smarter prefill for cold tenants — track as separate epic.
Coordinate with Dedicated team to reuse tenant pacing logic for reserved pools where isolation expectations differ.
